title: Wall Street muscles higher despite more swings for AI stocks
source_used: Associated Press (text read via LancasterOnline, which carries the AP wire)
key_facts: US stock indexes rose on Thursday 15 Oct 2026: S&P 500 up 0.3%, Dow up 556 points or 1.1%, Nasdaq up 0.1%.
The S&P 500 erased an early loss and closed nearer its all-time high from last week.
An AI-stock sell-off that began on Wall Street on Wednesday sent South Korea's Kospi down 7.6% and Japan's Nikkei 225 down 4.9%.
Marsh & McLennan rose 4.6%, Kimberly-Clark 4.7% and Bank of New York Mellon 3.2% on profit news.
Worries are rising over how resilient AI spending is because many companies borrowed to pay for data centres and chips as global bond yields hit multi-year highs.
Nvidia fell 1.8% and was the heaviest weight on the market.
quote_evidence: U.S. stock indexes muscled higher Thursday, led by companies delivering bigger profits.
But data centers and AI chips cost money, and many companies have been borrowing the cash to get them.
Treasury yields fell despite another report saying U.S. inflation is worsening.
why_it_matters_hint: US stocks held up on earnings even as AI shares kept swinging.
notes: AP page blocked (403); AP wire text read on LancasterOnline. Text read was cut before the end of the wire, so only the first part is used.
